fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled first byte of each 2-byte chunk header becomes the chunk size; the pointer advances by 2 bytes, so the second header byte is padding.
If the attacker's chunk_size exceeds apdu->resplen, resplen is left unchanged (equal to the full remaining buffer size left), so memcpy below writes resplen bytes.
Writes apdu->resplen bytes into apdu->resp, which points into the stack buffer of cac_cac1_get_certificate; the write size is attacker-controlled via the chunk size.
resplen is set to the full remaining buffer size (4096 when out_buf==NULL, or 100 when called from cac_populate_cac1), not to the requested len, so the fuzz reader may write more than len bytes.

On the break path (SW1 != 0x63), left is decremented by len (the requested amount), not by the actual bytes written (apdu.resplen), so the computed result r = size - left can exceed the actual data written.
r is computed as size minus the (incorrectly decremented) left; when left is under-decremented relative to the bytes actually written, r overstates the valid data length.

When out_buf was NULL, r bytes are copied from the 4096-byte stack buffer buf; if r exceeds the number of bytes actually written into buf, this reads uninitialized stack memory, and if r exceeds 4096 it reads past the stack buffer (stack-buffer-overflow READ).
The inflated r is returned as val_len; val points to the malloc'd copy of the over-read stack data, propagating the corrupted length into the certificate parsing below.
cert_len inherits the inflated val_len, so the subsequent memcpy(priv->cache_buf, cert_ptr, cert_len) reads beyond the allocated val buffer, completing the out-of-bounds read chain.
